evaluations.evidence: view a list of sponsors
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes viewing sponsors but lacks an explicit story to create/manage sponsor entities (beyond assigning sponsors to events). Without sponsor creation/maintenance, the sponsor list cannot be reliably populated.

evaluations.evidence: view a list of user profiles
evaluations.rationale: Complementary capability exists to create accounts (user registration) and update profiles, enabling a list of profiles to be populated and maintained.

evaluations.evidence: email all the trainers at once from the website
evaluations.rationale: Requires a defined way to identify the set of trainers (trainer role assignment / trainer directory). Backlog has trainer-facing training-node features but no story establishing how users become/are managed as trainers.

evaluations.evidence: have a very clear map where the buildings and rooms are
evaluations.rationale: This can be implemented as content/UI without requiring a missing complementary CRUD capability evidenced elsewhere in the backlog.

evaluations.evidence: edit my training node myself
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes multiple stories implying training nodes exist and are presented; editing is a complementary capability to those training pages and does not expose a missing prerequisite beyond training content existence, which is implied by the training feature set.

evaluations.evidence: limit to one registration per day per authenticated user
evaluations.rationale: Depends on a training registration capability, but the backlog lacks an explicit story for registering for a training (only waitlist, schedule, and viewing signed-up trainings).

evaluations.evidence: admin view that helps track registration status for each attendee ... attended, refunded, no show
evaluations.rationale: Tracking these statuses presumes a workflow to set/update registration status (attended/refunded/no-show). Backlog has refunding sponsorship money but no explicit story to mark attendance/no-show or to update training registration status.

evaluations.evidence: be added to a training waitlist
evaluations.rationale: Waitlisting presumes a primary training registration process and capacity management; backlog lacks an explicit story to register for a training.

evaluations.evidence: must accept the cancellation terms with a checkbox
evaluations.rationale: Cancellation terms acceptance is part of a registration/cancellation workflow, but the backlog lacks an explicit training registration and explicit training cancellation story.

evaluations.evidence: tie in a cancellation deadline to whatever registration / cancellation workflow exists
evaluations.rationale: Backlog references a registration/cancellation workflow but does not include an explicit story for training registration or training cancellation, which are prerequisites for enforcing deadlines.

evaluations.evidence: add to "my schedule" if there is a schedule feature on the site
evaluations.rationale: Adding items to a personal schedule implies the existence of a personal schedule feature (create/view/manage). Backlog includes viewing the global schedule but no explicit story to view/manage a user's personal schedule.

evaluations.evidence: see which trainings I have signed up for
evaluations.rationale: Requires the ability to sign up/register for trainings, but no explicit training registration story exists in the backlog.

evaluations.evidence: view ... shows all attendee information
evaluations.rationale: Trainer access to attendee info presumes attendees can register for trainings and that attendee lists are captured; backlog lacks an explicit training registration story.

evaluations.evidence: admin view where all trainee information is shown and can be filtered to show a single training session
evaluations.rationale: Filtering trainee info by training session presumes trainees are registered to trainings and that registrations exist; backlog lacks an explicit training registration story.

evaluations.evidence: link to register for class
evaluations.rationale: Story requires a registration capability for trainings/classes, but the backlog does not include an explicit story to register for a training.

evaluations.evidence: register now link
evaluations.rationale: Requires training registration functionality, which is not explicitly present in the backlog.

evaluations.evidence: training landing page ... list of all training offerings and promote call for trainings
evaluations.rationale: A landing page and call-for-trainings promotion can be implemented as content/navigation without a missing complementary capability evidenced elsewhere.

evaluations.evidence: link on the home page to a list of training options
evaluations.rationale: Complementary capability exists to present training options via training pages/landing pages; no missing prerequisite is evidenced.

evaluations.evidence: find out where the coding lounge is and what time it is open
evaluations.rationale: Can be satisfied via informational content; backlog does not evidence a missing complementary capability required to implement it.

evaluations.evidence: refund sponsorship money that was processed via stripe
evaluations.rationale: Refunding presumes a Stripe payment processing flow for sponsorships; backlog includes paying for sponsorships but does not explicitly cover capturing/recording Stripe charge identifiers needed for refunds (i.e., end-to-end payment-to-refund lifecycle).

evaluations.evidence: link ... to become a $350 level sponsor
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes identifying/paying for $350 company sponsorship, supporting the linked action.

evaluations.evidence: See a list of attendees associated with this company
evaluations.rationale: Requires a way to associate attendees/users with a company/sponsor organization; backlog has linking attendees to sponsorship page but not explicit creation/maintenance of attendee-to-company association.

evaluations.evidence: identify myself as and pay for a $350 company sponsorship
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes sponsorship payment steps/pages and card charging, enabling the sponsorship purchase flow.

evaluations.evidence: create and maintain venues
evaluations.rationale: Complementary read capability exists (view venue details), forming a coherent CRUD subset for venues.

evaluations.evidence: view venue details
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes venue creation/maintenance, enabling venue details to exist.

evaluations.evidence: see a list of the sessions associated with sponsor attendees
evaluations.rationale: Requires (1) sponsor-attendee association and (2) attendee-session association (e.g., which sessions an attendee is presenting/attending). Backlog lacks explicit stories establishing these associations.

evaluations.evidence: See a payment page ... third step of the registration process
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes selecting sponsorship options and entering payment information/charging card, supporting the payment step.

evaluations.evidence: assign sponsors to events, trainings and summits
evaluations.rationale: Assigning sponsors presumes sponsors exist as manageable entities; backlog lacks an explicit story for administrators to create/maintain sponsors (separate from purchasing sponsorship).

evaluations.evidence: see all events, trainings and summits that a sponsor is sponsoring
evaluations.rationale: Requires sponsors to exist and be assigned to items; assignment exists, but sponsor entity creation/maintenance is not explicitly covered, risking inability to populate sponsor pages consistently.

evaluations.evidence: Enter payment information and have my card charged
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes sponsorship selection and payment page steps, forming a coherent payment flow.

evaluations.evidence: link BADCamp attendees to my sponsorship page
evaluations.rationale: Requires a defined mechanism to associate attendees with a sponsor/company; backlog lacks explicit stories for creating/managing those attendee-company links (beyond this sponsor desire).

evaluations.evidence: update my user profile
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes account creation via user registration, enabling profiles to exist and be updated.

evaluations.evidence: sign up for the BADCamp newsletter
evaluations.rationale: Can be implemented as a standalone subscription capability; backlog does not evidence a missing complementary prerequisite.

evaluations.evidence: tag my blog posts
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes creating blog posts, enabling tagging to apply to existing posts.

evaluations.evidence: create blog posts
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes reading the blog and WYSIWYG support, forming a coherent create/read content set.

evaluations.evidence: read the blog
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes creating blog posts, enabling blog content to exist.

evaluations.evidence: sponsor a summit
evaluations.rationale: Sponsoring a summit implies a purchase/commitment workflow for summit sponsorship; backlog has general sponsorship payment flows but no explicit story connecting summit sponsorship selection/payment to the summit sponsorship listing features.

evaluations.evidence: register for a summit
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes viewing seats left, viewing summit details, seeing summits signed up for, and coordinator attendee lists, forming a coherent summit registration feature set.

evaluations.evidence: get detailed directions to the summit venue
evaluations.rationale: Requires summit-to-venue/location data. Backlog has venue management and viewing venue details, but no explicit story to associate a summit with a venue/location.

evaluations.evidence: see what summits I'm signed up for
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes summit registration, enabling sign-ups to exist for later viewing.

evaluations.evidence: see a list of attendees signed up for my summit
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes summit registration, enabling attendee lists to be generated.

evaluations.evidence: list basic information about my summit
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes viewing summit details and lists of summits, which rely on summit information being entered.

evaluations.evidence: list sponsors for my summit
evaluations.rationale: Listing summit sponsors requires a way to associate sponsors with a summit. Backlog has assigning sponsors to events/trainings/summits, but lacks explicit sponsor entity creation/maintenance, risking inability to populate sponsor lists.

evaluations.evidence: list an agenda for my summit
evaluations.rationale: Agenda can be created/managed as summit content; backlog does not evidence a missing complementary prerequisite for agenda listing.

evaluations.evidence: see how many seats are left for the summit
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes summit registration, which provides the basis for seat counts/remaining capacity.

evaluations.evidence: see specific details on summits
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes summit info entry and related summit features (registration, seats left, directions), supporting a complete summit detail experience at a feature level.

evaluations.evidence: see a list of all the summits
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes summit information entry, enabling summits to exist for listing.

evaluations.evidence: learn about sponsorship levels
evaluations.rationale: Learning about sponsorship levels implies those levels are defined/managed somewhere; backlog includes purchasing specific levels but lacks an explicit story to create/maintain sponsorship levels/content.

evaluations.evidence: use a WYSIWYG editor for all long-form content
evaluations.rationale: Supports content creation/maintenance stories (e.g., blog posts, summit info) and does not expose a missing complementary capability.

evaluations.evidence: Link to my sponsorship profile from my job listings
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes sponsors posting jobs and sponsors having/personalizing sponsorship pages, enabling linking between them.

evaluations.evidence: learn about posting jobs as a sponsor and contact the sponsorship person
evaluations.rationale: Informational/contact capability can stand alone; backlog includes job posting by sponsors, aligning with this informational step.

evaluations.evidence: post a job
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes viewing the job board, providing complementary read capability for posted jobs.

evaluations.evidence: view the job board
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes posting jobs, enabling job listings to exist for viewing.

evaluations.evidence: assign a room to a time slot and a location
evaluations.rationale: Assigning rooms/time slots/locations presumes rooms and time slots exist as manageable entities. Backlog lacks explicit stories to create/maintain rooms and time slots (venue CRUD exists, but not rooms/time slots).

evaluations.evidence: see the schedule
evaluations.rationale: Viewing a schedule depends on schedule population (rooms/time slots/session placements). Backlog includes assigning rooms to time slots but lacks explicit creation/maintenance of rooms and time slots, risking inability to build a complete schedule.

evaluations.evidence: see the final list of sessions approved
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes submitting sessions and accepting/approving sessions, enabling an approved list to exist.

evaluations.evidence: bulk approve sessions as accepted
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes session submission and acceptance marking, providing the necessary context for bulk approval.

evaluations.evidence: mark a session as accepted
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes session submission, enabling sessions to exist to be accepted.

evaluations.evidence: receive a notification when sessions have been evaluated
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes session submission and acceptance/evaluation actions, providing the triggering events for notifications.

evaluations.evidence: receive a notification when I submit a session
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes session submission, enabling a submission event to trigger a notification.

evaluations.evidence: edit my session
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes session submission/registration to speak, enabling sessions to exist for later editing.

evaluations.evidence: register to speak ... submit a session
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes submitting a session, editing, and notifications, forming a coherent speaker submission feature set.

evaluations.evidence: submit a session ... get my session evaluated
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes acceptance/approval actions and evaluation notifications, supporting the evaluation lifecycle.

evaluations.evidence: personalize my sponsorship page
evaluations.rationale: Personalizing a sponsorship page presumes a sponsorship profile/page exists for the sponsor; backlog lacks an explicit story to create/maintain sponsor profiles/entities (as opposed to paying for sponsorship).

evaluations.evidence: see a list of all the summits that include when they are
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes summit basic information entry and summit listing, enabling a dated list of summits.

evaluations.evidence: offered several choices of idividual sponsorship on the second page of registration
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes subsequent payment steps and charging card, supporting the multi-step sponsorship registration flow.

evaluations.evidence: find a link in the menu that links to the registration form
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes the registration form itself, enabling the menu link to point to an existing capability.

evaluations.evidence: fill out a user registration form
evaluations.rationale: Account creation is a foundational capability and is complemented by profile viewing/updating stories.

evaluations.evidence: find session information
evaluations.rationale: Backlog includes session submission and approved session lists, providing session content to be found.
